# The patch {#sec-patch}

One optional ALTREP method:

```c
/* R_ext/Altrep.h */
typedef SEXP (*R_altvec_Extract_array_subset_method_t)(SEXP x, SEXP subs,
                                                       SEXP dim, SEXP call);
void R_set_altvec_Extract_array_subset_method(R_altrep_class_t cls,
                         R_altvec_Extract_array_subset_method_t fun);
#define R_ALTREP_HAS_EXTRACT_ARRAY_SUBSET 1
```

In `src/main/subset.c`, `MatrixSubset()` and `ArraySubset()` normalize
the subscripts as they always have. Just before the element loop, if `x`
is ALTREP, they offer the method what they hold: a list with one vector
of 1-based positions per dimension (`NA` allowed), and the array's `dim`.
The method returns the values, or C `NULL` to decline.

## What R keeps

- Normalizing subscripts: negative, logical, character, missing, zero.
- Bounds checking. The method only sees in-range positions or `NA`.
- `dim`, `dimnames` and `drop` on the result.
- Checking what the method returns: type, length, no attributes.

## What does not change

- **Existing classes.** The default method returns `NULL`, so compact
  sequences, deferred strings, and every package class that
  does not set the method behave exactly as before.
- **The ABI.** R allocates each class's method table and packages only
  call setters, so adding a method moves nothing a compiled package can
  see.
- **Package sources.** A package opts in behind
  `#ifdef R_ALTREP_HAS_EXTRACT_ARRAY_SUBSET` and builds on any R. Every
  table in this book is that: one altarr source, two builds of R.
- **Cost for everyone else.** A non-ALTREP array pays one `ALTREP(x)`
  test. An ALTREP class without the method pays that and a short list.

## Why not reuse `Extract_subset`

R could build the linear index for the block and call the existing
method. That needs no new API, but it allocates an index as long as the
result for every ALTREP array, including classes that then decline, and
the class has to recover the rectangle from the offsets. The new method
passes the per-dimension subscripts R already has.

## Size and state

Six files, about 100 lines added and 3 removed, with a NEWS entry. It is
kept applying to current R-devel in this repository
([`variants/array-subset`](https://github.com/mdsumner/r-variants/tree/main/variants/array-subset)),
checked weekly. `make check` passes on the patched build. altarr's tests
and a minimal test package cover declining, misbehaving methods, wrappers,
dimnames, `NA`, negative, logical and character subscripts, zero extents,
and `gctorture`.

## Try it

```sh
docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/mdsumner/r-variants:array-subset
```

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("hypertidy/altarr@exp/r-hook")
library(altarr)
x <- altarr_zarr_v2(altarr_example_zarr())
y <- x[1:40, 1:20, 1:3]
altarr_stats(x)[c("array_subset", "elt", "fetch_calls")]   # 1, 0, 1
```

The `baseline` image is stock R-devel at a nearby revision; the same lines
there give `array_subset` 0 and thousands of `elt` reads.

## Questions the patch leaves for R core

- A feature macro, as here, or an `R_VERSION` test?
- May the method return an ALTREP object, a lazy result? The patch
  neither forbids nor promises it.
- Would a small test package under `tests/Pkgs` be welcome, since base R
  has no class that implements the method?
- Should the dispatch function be exported, so wrapper classes in
  packages can forward the method as R's own wrapper does?

## What is not in this book yet

- **Sparse stores.** altarr's main branch can skip chunks a store never
  wrote, from a chunk index. The method lives on the `exp/r-hook` branch,
  which predates that work; the two need joining before a sparse chapter
  can compare builds.
- **GDAL.** `GDAL7::as_altarr()` on a multidimensional array and on a
  COG's overviews.
- **A public Icechunk repository** in place of the toy in @sec-icechunk.
- **Kerchunk JSON and Parquet references**, alongside the VirtualiZarr
  store in @sec-virtual.
